beats.narration_en: Why is this guardrail covered in spinning yellow rollers?
It's a rolling barrier made in South Korea for dangerous curves.
Hit a plain steel rail and it scrapes and drags at the car.
These rollers are barrels of tough foam on steel posts.
When a car slides into them they spin instead of scraping.
The foam squashes to soak up the hit.
And the spinning turns part of the crash into rotation.
So the car keeps rolling forward and is steered back toward its lane.
One version passed a sixty-two mile an hour crash test for American roads.
Korea already has more than sixty miles of them.
That's why some sharp curves are lined with spinning yellow rollers.
